routine: C0/5B95 actor-vs-actor 1-tile-ahead collision (+ edge clamps C0/5B63-5B8C)
corrections: CALLER IS WRONG: the spec says C0/5129 (opcode 0xA0) calls 5B95 and does the $EE+=0x30 nudge. It does NOT. C0/5129 is a sibling position-compare routine that never calls 5B95. The real caller exercised in the trace is C0/5170 (trace lines 16671->16672: 'C0 5170' then 'C0 5B95'), and the 'BCC clear else $EE+=0x30' pattern lives at C0/5170-517A (JSR $5B95 / BCC $517C / LDA $EE / CLC / ADC #$30 / STA $EE). Note 5B95 has NINE callers (C0/4FBD,504F,50FC,5170,51F4,5293,5329,53DC,54C8), not one. The 'opcode 0xA0' attribution is unverified and likely incorrect.

'DORMANT in the trace' is misleading. 5B95 IS executed (trace 16672-16680): it runs 5B95->5B97->5B99->5B9C->5BA0->5BA3->5BA5(BEQ)->5B9E(CLC)->5B9F(RTS). It reaches the gate at 5BA0 and bails CLC=movable at 5B9E because $1C80,X&0x02 is clear. So it is reached-and-gated-off every frame, not dormant. (Conclusion that the 4 box handlers are oracle-UNTESTED is still correct.)

INDEX STRIDE / $6D annotation is wrong-or-unresolved: spec's wramReads says '$6D = mover actor index (0x80-strided)'. But inside 5B95 the scan index X is count*2 (LDA $7F2000; ASL; TAX) and is used to read $0F00,X/$1100,X/$1800,X/$1880,X/$1B01,X AND compared via CPX $6D (5BD7). For the CPX self-skip to be meaningful, $6D must be in the SAME count*2 space here -- which conflicts with disasm/notes/field_tick.md (lines 40,94: per-actor WRAM is 0x80-strided, the +2 is only a loop counter). This is a genuine byte-exact UNRESOLVED hazard; the wramReads '0x80-strided' label overstates certainty and is internally inconsistent with the count*2 usage. Do not port the table indexing until this is pinned.

$01D9 is an ABSOLUTE address, not direct-page. In the edge bodies 5B63/5B79 the opcodes are '8D D9 01'=STA $01D9 (abs) and 'CD D9 01'=CMP $01D9 (abs). The spec's phrasing '$01D9 (DP=$1D00 => $01D9)' implies a DP-relative resolve; it is DP-independent (always writes $7E:01D9). Result is the same but the reasoning is wrong.
5B8D ($EB sign predicate) IS pinnable: it is called from C0/304F (JSR $5B8D). Spec said its caller 'was not pinned in this pass.'

Minor: handler 0 entry is C0/5BFA (verified by raw table bytes FA 5B). A naive disasm starting at 5C00 mis-decodes the tail of handler 0 as a phantom 5th handler -- the real handlers are exactly the 4 table entries {5BFA,5C20,5C47,5C6D}, no 5th. The spec's table is correct; flag only so the porter aligns at 5BFA.
crossChecks: Re-disassembled C0/5B63-5C90 independently (DP=$1D00 for the four edge clamps; DP=$0100 for the 5B95 cluster). Confirmed the 5BF2 pointer table raw bytes = FA 5B 20 5C 47 5C 6D 5C -> {$5BFA,$5C20,$5C47,$5C6D}. Re-aligned handler 0 at 5BFA (the 5C00 listing was a mis-aligned tail).

Re-derived every edge-clamp carry sense from CMP (carry SET = blocked because 9175 does BCS->skip-store): 5B86 LEFT blocked iff $1D1A>=posX($1801,X); 5B79 RIGHT blocked iff posX>=$1D1B; 5B71 UP blocked iff (u8)($1D1C+1)>=posY($1881,X); 5B63 DOWN blocked iff posY>=(u8)($1D1D+1). Confirmed 9175 dispatch: Xvel<0->5B86, Xvel>0->5B79, Yvel<0->5B71, Yvel>0->5B63.

Cross-checked src/player.c: edgeLeft uses '==' not '>=' (BUG1 confirmed); edgeUp/edgeDown labels are swapped vs ROM bodies AND dispatched on the wrong Y sign (BUG2 confirmed); Y bounds mismatched -- player.c uses $1D1D on the up label and $1D1C on the down label, both with down-style '>=' comparison (BUG3 confirmed). edgeRight matches ROM exactly. All three spec-claimed bugs verified TRUE.

Trace disasm/boot_trace_play.txt: confirmed it is a PC-only stream (fields: bank pc dp m x dbr), no operand values -- so 1D1A-1D1D bound values are NOT observable there. Followed 5B95 live: enters via 5170, hits gate 5BA0/5BA3/5BA5, branches to 5B9E CLC RTS, returns to 5173 with carry clear (BCC taken, $EE NOT nudged). Confirms gate-off path and identifies the true caller.

Verified handler one's-complement: all 4 handlers use EOR #$FFFF (5C05,5C37/5C52/5C61/5C84) on the negative-delta branch and CMP #$0100 / BCS for the |delta|<$0100 test (spec correct). Verified the carry-uninitialized-on-first-SBC hazard at handler entry (5BFA: LDA $1880,X; SBC $DD with no preceding SEC/CLC; LDX/BIT before the JSR do not touch carry) -- spec's HAZARD flag is legitimate.

Cross-checked assets/engine.py solid_at/move_player and disasm/notes/field_tick.md: engine.py models ONLY tile-property collision (solid_at) and has no actor-vs-actor model, so it cannot validate the box handlers. field_tick.md (lines 40,94) states per-actor WRAM is 0x80-strided with a separate +2 loop counter -- which is what exposed the $6D/count*2 stride inconsistency in the spec.
